answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a time-locked bond before it may earn, like tending an orchard where every tree must be planted and watered before it bears fruit. Fake identities multiply cheaply, but a bond that only matures after sustained, verifiable work makes mass cloning unprofitable: the attacker pays for every copy while honest agents reach their zenith through accumulated reputation. The bond pool becomes a shared haven — misbehaving agents forfeit their stake to compensate victims, so trust grows from skin in the game, not from mere claims of identity.
